title: Saved by Grace, Unto Good Works
chapterRef: Chapter 2: Saved by Grace, Unto Good Works

hero.mood: an open doorway, not a parking space
hero.alt: A sunlit open doorway at the end of an empty parking lot.

hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
A bad week doesn't un-adopt you. If you failed, return to grace. Confess it, receive mercy, and get up. Your standing with God was settled before your first step, and it isn't revoked by a slow week.

If you can't take a step, your task is honesty and one trusted believer. Then read "A Word to New Believers" and "What Changes When Grace Launches You." Direction, not perfection.

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 2
read.body:
Open to Chapter 2, "Saved by Grace, Unto Good Works." Read "Ephesians 2:8-10 in Plain Sight" and "Created for Good Works." Then read "The Scoreboard, and the Fear That Action Means Earning," because it names the two ditches.

Some of us work nonstop and still feel insecure, afraid that obeying means trying to earn God. Others barely move and call it rest. Chapter 2 says both have missed the gospel. Chapter 2 keeps both halves of Ephesians 2 in front of you so you don't lose either one.

Read it slowly. If you've lived in one of those ditches, you'll recognize it. Then come back.

read.quote: Grace is not a parking space.
prompts: Which ditch do I drift toward: earning, or passivity?

pulse.heading: The pulse: gift first, then walk
pulse.body:
Earning asks, "What must I produce so God will accept me?" Fruit asks, "Since God has accepted me, how do I walk as His workmanship?"

That's Chapter 2. Abraham believed before he performed. His righteousness was counted to him by faith. Motion followed mercy. It never purchased it.

So you don't obey to get loved. You obey because you already are.

verses.text: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.”

prompts: Say it in your own words: what's the difference between earning and fruit?

nameIt.heading: Name it: read it out loud
nameIt.body:
Chapter 2 asks you to read Ephesians 2:8-10 out loud. Do it now, even if it's a whisper. Hear both halves. Not by works. Created for good works.

Most of us forget one half. Some of us forget we're saved by grace and work like orphans. Some of us forget we're created for good works and rest like spectators. Be honest about which one you forget.

bookRef.chapter: Chapter 2: Saved by Grace, Unto Good Works
bookRef.section: Ephesians 2:8-10 in Plain Sight; Reflection Questions

verses.text: For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.

prompts: When I think about obeying God this week, does my heart drift toward earning His love, or toward ignoring hard obedience because I'm already accepted?
Which half do I forget more: "not a result of works," or "created in Christ Jesus for good works"?
Where has "resting in grace" become a soft word for unused gifts?

build.heading: Build it: one plain good work
build.body:
God prepared good works beforehand. You still have to walk in them.

This isn't a scoreboard project. Pick one plain good work God has already made clear for this week. Think ordinary: a meal, an apology, a visit, honest work, a gift. Something nobody may ever post about.

And a word about diligence. Scripture honors hard work. Proverbs tells us how life usually goes under God. It isn't a promise of money for effort. Diligence isn't the enemy. Hustle as your identity is. Systems and plans are good servants. They make terrible masters.

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 2:

Write one good work God has already made plain for this week, not a scoreboard project. Do it as fruit of grace. Then thank Him that your acceptance was settled before the work began.

That last part matters. Don't skip the thank you. If you miss your date, set a new one within three days. Fruit is not foundation.

help.heading: Help: bring one answer, walk with one person
help.body:
Bring one answer to a trusted believer this week. Maybe it's which half of Ephesians 2 you forget.

Then think of someone who seems worn out, whether from trying too hard or from giving up. You don't need a sermon. Send them Ephesians 2:8-10 and one sentence about what it meant to you this week.

pray.heading: Pray it: thank Him first
pray.body:
Grace is a gift, not a paycheck. Start with thanks.

Father, thank You. I was dead and You made me alive. I didn't earn it, and I can't lose it by a bad week.

Thank You for preparing good works for me before I ever got here. Help me walk in this one: ____.

Keep me out of both ditches. Don't let me work to be loved, and don't let me rest my way out of obedience. In Jesus' name, amen.

review.heading: Review: living faith
review.body:
After your date, mark it: did it, not yet, or holy wait.

Guardrail from Chapter 2: Paul and James aren't fighting. Paul aims at people trying to earn. James aims at people with empty talk. Living faith shows itself. And the fruit of the Spirit isn't a performance chart. It's what grows in a life that's already His.

If you missed, hear this. Fruit is not foundation. A bad week does not un-adopt you. Rest, but don't disappear.
